evidence.claim_supported: The SSR renderer applies a module pipeline to every element start tag, and `domProps` is one of the registered server modules.
evidence.why_relevant: This shows `domProps` participates in server-side HTML generation for element tags.

evidence.claim_supported: The SSR tag renderer iterates the module list when building the opening tag, so the registered `domProps` module is executed during SSR output generation.
evidence.why_relevant: This shows where the server renderer invokes each module while serializing an element's start tag.

evidence.claim_supported: The SSR `domProps` module special-cases `textarea` `value` and turns it into a text child without filtering out falsy values such as `null`.
evidence.why_relevant: This is the code path that can place `null` into a textarea's rendered content.

evidence.claim_supported: Server-side rendering of string nodes converts non-raw text with `escape(String(node.text))`, so a `null` text child becomes the literal string `null`.
evidence.why_relevant: This explains why a textarea text child created from `null` is emitted as `null` in HTML.

evidence.claim_supported: Normal SSR attribute rendering suppresses falsy values, which contrasts with the textarea `domProps.value` path.
evidence.why_relevant: This provides surrounding behavior for ordinary attributes and helps isolate the textarea-specific `domProps` path.

prompt_summary: SSR server rendering includes a `domProps` module that special-cases `textarea` values by converting them into text children, and SSR string serialization will emit `null` as the literal text `null` when that child is not filtered out. Ordinary SSR attribute rendering already suppresses falsy values.
uncertainties: The snapshot shows the relevant SSR code path, but not the eventual fix or whether the intended change should happen in `dom-props.js` versus an upstream normalization step.
I did not inspect tests or external issue artifacts; this evidence only establishes the implementation context.
